title: Personal background; move to Idaho
description: Lillian Thompson provides her birth information and describes moving from Montana to Idaho in 1956 by car with her husband and three children, Harold and Marilyn among them.

title: Parents' history; family origins
description: She discusses her mother's maiden name and life in central Montana mining towns, her father's homesteading and blacksmith work in Montana, and her parents' marriage, birth dates, and deaths.

title: Siblings; husband's background
description: She names her sisters and brothers, including a half-brother and a brother killed in a Portland accident in 1967, then provides details about her husband Harold's birth in Greenfield, Missouri, and his farming and military service.

title: Children's lives; work history
description: She describes her three children's birth dates, marriages, and employment, including Harold's work at a furniture store and fire company, another son's lumber company position, and Marilyn's work as a waitress and nurse's aide.

title: Education; early employment
description: She explains that high school took thirteen years, describes earning fifteen dollars a month for housework as a girl, and participating in the National Youth Administration program doing typing and filing at school.

title: Farm labor; self-sufficiency
description: She recounts working on the family farm in Montana doing machinery operation, cooking, and gardening, emphasizing that girls performed the same labor as boys because parents could not afford hired help.

title: Hobbies; community organizations
description: She lists her hobbies including crocheting, quilting, and gardening, mentions belonging to the Princeton Club and homemakers club, and explains her limited involvement due to her husband's work and the distance to town.

title: Religious background; rural life reflection
description: She discusses raising her children Catholic and their drift from the church, then reflects on the peace and quiet of rural Elk River despite heavy snows and the contrast with her sister-in-law's urban California lifestyle.

title: Children's upbringing; work ethic
description: She compares her children's working youth to her own farm childhood, describing how they held jobs from age fourteen, learned mechanical skills, and developed responsibility without college education.

title: School recreation; transportation dangers
description: She recalls playing basketball and baseball in high school, riding horses five miles to school, walking home, and a traumatic incident where the family sled was nearly struck by a train while crossing tracks.

title: Family activities; community gatherings
description: She describes her children's involvement in school activities and Boy Scouts, family Fourth of July picnics in the mountains, Thanksgiving gatherings with shared meals, and the loss of such fellowship in modern times.

title: Community comparison; moving reception
description: She contrasts the helpful, down-to-earth people of Elk River with her previous community in Potlatch, where she felt unwelcome and received help from the mayor and local children when moving during an April snowstorm.

title: Courtship; military marriage
description: She details her three-month courtship with Harold, working at a ranch at the time of their marriage, her subsequent jobs at cleaners and photo shops, and living on army bases during his service.

title: Wartime separation; relocation decision
description: She describes her husband's overseas deployment to England, their son's birth while he was away, living with her mother, and the decision to move to Idaho based on her brother's encouragement and promise of higher wages, despite leaving a steady school cooking job in Montana.
